Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

suus

suus, sua, suum

pronoun (possessive, reflexive)

her (own), referring to the subject; his (own), referring to the subject; its (own), referring to the subject; his, her, its, their own; one’s own; their (own), referring to the subject

In this lexicon

  • her

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 4.1.4: nātālī suō ipsō diē; Catull. 3.5: oculīs suīs

  • his

    the recommended word · classical · Liv. 2.10.11: incolumis ad suōs trānāvit; Cic. Off. 3.59: invītat Canius postrīdiē familiārēs suōs

  • its

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Sen. 52: claviculīs suīs quasi manibus; Mart. 4.32.2: apis nectare clūsa suō

  • own

    the recommended word · classical · Liv. 2.32.9: singulīs membrīs suum cuique cōnsilium, suus sermō; Plaut. Stich. 1.2.76: suus rēx rēgīnae placet, a queen likes her own king (Lewis & Short)

  • their

    the recommended word · classical · Liv. 21.58.8: tegminibus suīs magis obrutī quam tēctī; Liv. 21.28.1: cantūque mōris suī

Examples

  • meī sunt ōrdinēs, mea dīscrīptiō, multae etiam istārum arborum meā manū sunt satae

    the rows are mine, the plan is mine, and many of those trees were planted with my own handCic. Sen. 59

    In the entry for own

  • singulīs membrīs suum cuique cōnsilium, suus sermō fuerit

    each limb had its own mind and its own voiceLiv. 2.32.9

    In the entry for own

  • āmittit meritō proprium quī aliēnum adpetit

    whoever grabs at what is another’s deserves to lose his ownPhaedr. 1.4.1
